AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
AbstractText.content: Chymase is a unique abundant secretory product of mast cells, and a potent chemoattractant for eosinophils, monocytes and neutrophils, but little is known of its influence on mast cell accumulation.

AbstractText.Label: EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH
AbstractText.content: Using mouse peritoneal inflammation model, cell migration assay and flowcytometry analysis, we investigated role of chymase in recruiting mast cells.

AbstractText.Label: KEY RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The results showed that chymase induced up to 5.4-fold increase in mast cell numbers in mouse peritoneum. Inhibitors of chymase, heat-inactivation of the enzyme, sodium cromoglycate and terfenadine, and pretreatment of mice with anti-ICAM-1, anti-L-selectin, anti-CD11a and anti-CD18 antibodies dramatically diminished chymase-induced mast cell accumulation, implicating that the event is dependent on chymase enzymatic activity, and activation of adhesion molecules. In addition, chymase provoked up to 1.8 and 2.2-fold increased serotonin (P = 0.006) and eotaxin (P = 0.003) release in peritoneum of mice. Since serotonin, eotaxin and RANTES can induce marked mast cell accumulation, the indirect mechanisms may also contribute to chymase-induced mast cell accumulation. Moreover, induction of trans-endothelium migration of mast cells in vitro indicates chymase acts as a chemoattractant.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION AND IMPLICATIONS
AbstractText.content: In conclusion, induction of mast cell accumulation by chymase implies further that chymase is a major proinflammatory mediator of mast cells. The mast cell accumulation provoked by chymase, a major mast cell granule product suggests a novel self-amplification mechanism of mast cell accumulation in allergic inflammation. Mast cell stabilizer as well as inhibitors of chymase may be useful for treatment of allergic disorders.
